claims.behavior: Whether a `queue-operation` line carries the queued text at all is OPERATION-DEPENDENT, and the dependence lives in the call sites rather than in the line builder. One function builds every such line - o(op, content, reason) { {type:"queue-operation", operation, timestamp, sessionId, ...content!==undefined && {content}, ...reason!==undefined && {reason}} } at 162031901 - and `content` and `reason` are CONDITIONAL SPREADS, so a key exists only when the caller passed the argument. The enqueue entries (162035115, 162035826) and the remove and popAll sites pass typeof value==="string" ? value : void 0, while the dequeue sites call o("dequeue") BARE. That set is closed: the quoted string "dequeue" occurs exactly FOUR times in the 2.1.258 binary, all four bare one-argument calls inside the queue module (162037953, 162038474, 162038598, 162039004), so a dequeue line can never gain a content key. Only the remove site passes a third argument, so `reason` can ride only a remove line. The line reaches disk through insertQueueOperation, which appends the raw object with no envelope spread (166122777), which is also why a queue line carries no cwd, version or uuid. Measured 2026-09-04 over the whole projects root (one row per physical queue-operation line, grouped by the `operation` value; 'content present' = the top-level key exists): 13,868 lines, 0 unparseable, 0 non-string content values - `enqueue` 6,938/6,938 (100%), `popAll` 109/109 (100%), `remove` 2,483/3,279 (75.7%) and `dequeue` 0/3,542 (never). A `dequeue` therefore carries nothing to search. The remove shortfall is a corpus-age artefact rather than live behavior: bucketing the 32 sessions that carry remove lines by the highest version stamped on their records, all 24 sessions at 2.1.206 or later log removes WITH content and all 8 at 2.1.202 or earlier log them without, with no mixed session - so at the audited binary a remove carries the text exactly like an enqueue. A `reason` is rarer still: 221 of the 3,279 removes carry one (absorbed_mid_turn 209, delivered_to_agent 12). The writer's operation vocabulary has a fifth member the corpus has never seen: o("popOne", value-if-string) at 162041776, zero occurrences corpus-wide.
claims.depends: csift assigns no label to a content-less queue line and renders the label zone as `[enqueue]` or `[remove - <reason>]`; a `dequeue` can be paired with its `enqueue` only by ordering and text, never by an id, since the builder puts no join key on the line. The conditional-spread shape is why csift must treat a missing `content` key as 'this operation carries nothing' rather than as an empty string, and why the promoted leaf user.queued exists only for the content-bearing operations.

Measured 2026-09-03 over 4,751 turn_duration records corpus-wide, 143 carry the field as a number with values 1 through 13 (histogram 1:61, 2:33, 3:18, 4:10, 5:6, 6:3, 7:4, 8:2, 9:2, 10:1, 11:1, 12:1, 13:1) and the value 0 never appears; pendingWorkflowCount likewise never 0 (1:231, 2:11, 3:2). The 2026-09-02 pass counted 136 numeric occurrences over the same range with the same absence of 0, and noted that a bare-key string search over-counts badly (398 lines contain the key name, the difference being escaped prose). What the number counts is the harness's own live task registry at that instant: gje (180033593) admits a backgrounded task whose status is running AND a terminal task not yet notified, plus any task named by a still-queued task-notification. It is therefore not a launch-and-return ledger, and a transcript replay of launches against completions cannot reconstruct it.
claims.depends: any consumer reading the field must treat an absent key as 0. csift's promoted turn-duration excerpt (src/search/record_text.rs) obeys that by construction: it appends pendingBackgroundAgentCount and pendingWorkflowCount only when the key is present and numeric, so it never fabricates a 0 the harness did not write. Beyond that the field must not be read as a count of open async work a transcript can reproduce: the number includes registry state a transcript never records (terminal-but-unnotified tasks, tasks whose notification is still queued), so csift's own launched-but-unreturned replay (the BgState lifecycle in src/live/background.rs) answers a different question and the two are not cross-validating instruments.

claims.behavior: Claude Code writes a `type:"system"` / `subtype:"away_summary"` record whose top-level `content` is ALWAYS a string: the record factory takes one string parameter and mints {type, subtype:"away_summary", content, timestamp, uuid, isMeta:false} with no message key (166031203), and the shipped SDK schema types content as a required string (158632124). It is the recap of what happened while the operator was away, and it is generated WHILE THE WINDOW IS BLURRED, not on return: the controller arms a timeout that fires only if the window is still blurred (181823457), and the delay is Math.min(remote_delay, cache_ttl * 0.8) where the remote delay reads a config gate defaulting to 180,000 ms and floored at 30,000 ms (181821222, 181823267). The five-minute constant in the same file gates only the return-to-session TELEMETRY event, not the recap (181823575). The text is model-generated by a separate side query rather than templated - the query denies every tool with the message 'Away summary cannot use tools', runs with maxTurns 1 and skips the cache write and the transcript, and truncates its result at 400 characters (168867635) - and the whole feature is config-gated behind `awaySummaryEnabled` (181824639). The trailing suffix ' (disable recaps in /config)' is a first-few-recaps-per-CONTROLLER-INSTANCE nudge, not an early-version artefact and not a per-session counter: the counter is a private field on the controller instance compared against 3 (181822818), and the hook creates that instance with a lazy initializer per mount (181824639), so the nudge restarts whenever the controller is remounted. Measured 2026-09-04 over the whole projects root (one row per matching line): 1,683 records, content a string on 1,683 of 1,683, 1,640 of them distinct, content length min/median/p99/max = 76/219/313/8,333 characters. Only two records exceed 428 characters and they are stamped 2.1.170 and 2.1.177, so the 8,333-character maximum is a pre-cap historical bound rather than a live one. The suffix appears on 192 records spanning 2.1.150 to 2.1.259: within a transcript it is on 41/41, 32/33 and 24/25 of the recaps at positions 1, 2 and 3, and ALSO on 95 of the 1,584 recaps at position 4 or later - a distribution only the per-instance counter explains.
claims.depends: csift promotes it to the gated leaf `harness.meta.away-summary` and matches on the VERBATIM `content` (a raw byte substring, so no synthesized marker is needed); it is the most valuable promoted prose, and because it is model-written it must never be presented as operator text. The record is also not evidence about when the operator returned: it is written during the blur, so its timestamp marks roughly the idle delay after the last activity, not a return.

claims.behavior: An away recap is a `type:"system"` / `subtype:"away_summary"` record built by one constructor (166031203) carrying content, timestamp, uuid and isMeta:false and NO `message{}` object. The recap text is pushed onto the same in-memory transcript array the REPL keeps (181822892), the array the human's own messages are appended to (180710536), so it really is a member of the conversation the query normalizes. The builder that turns that array into API messages then drops it: the first statement of the message-build loop skips any record for which LP holds (165959679), and LP holds for a progress record, for a virtual or api-error placeholder, and for a `type:"system"` record whose subtype is not `local_command` (165953664); the single surviving system subtype is checked by UWt (165947398) and survives only by being re-minted as a user message. The request body maps only the survivors' `message.role` and `message.content` (165407936), so a recap can never appear in a request and a record with no `message{}` could not be mapped at all. The recap itself is produced by a separate one-turn sub-query with querySource away_summary, tools denied and skipTranscript true (168868261), whose own messages are never persisted; the timer is armed only when the awaySummaryEnabled setting is on (181824717) and fires only while the terminal is blurred (181823457), behind a skip chain (181821805) that bails on a stale cache, a rate limit, a draft input, pending background work or a pending wakeup. Corpus, measured 2026-09-04 over every transcript under the projects root: 1,682 recap records in 41 files, all 1,682 testable; exactly 1 recurs later in its own file and the record carrying it is a later `type:"user"` record - a human quoting it back, not the harness delivering it - so 1,681 of 1,682 never re-appear anywhere downstream. 192 of the 1,682 end with the writer's literal ` (disable recaps in /config)` suffix, which the writer appends only to the first three recaps of a session instance (the cap constant is 3, at 181820261).
claims.depends: csift promotes the record to the LLM-invisible leaf `harness.meta.away-summary` and words it as shown in the UI, not in the surviving conversation; the leaf is gated, so a bare scan, a bare role selector and a flagless census never parse it. With the drop predicate located, that wording is no longer an inference from a census: csift can name the mechanism - the harness removes the record when it builds the API messages, and only a `local_command` system record survives that filter - and keep the recurrence census as corroboration. Treating a model-generated recap as delivered context would inflate every accounting of what the assistant actually received. The doc comment at src/model/taxonomy.rs still embeds the stale 1,196/1,198 figure and should be restamped in the same pass.

claims.behavior: At Claude Code 2.1.258 a stop_hook_summary record and a turn_duration record are written as a pair at each turn end, stop_hook_summary first, with the turn_duration record naming it as parentUuid. The pairing comes out of one turn-end guard in the REPL turn runner (181625968, `let Xo=this.guard.end(To)` and `if(Xo){...}`): the Stop-hook stage has already emitted the stop_hook_summary earlier in the same query loop under `if(xt>0){...yield wUn(...)}` (164633948), and the turn-end branch then appends `B_t(...)` (call 181626578, constructor `function B_t(e,n,r,o,d){return{type:"system",subtype:"turn_duration",...}}` at 166030930), so the persistence entry Rw computes the running chain leaf as the stop_hook_summary uuid before insertMessageChain (166113249) and the envelope stamps it as parentUuid. NEITHER subtype is a safe turn counter on its own, but not for the reason previously recorded. stop_hook_summary is absent when no Stop hook produced a progress message, because xt stays 0 and the emission gate never fires. turn_duration is NOT suppressed by the showTurnDuration user setting: a full enumeration of all 17 occurrences of that literal in the 2.1.258 binary finds it only in the settings schema and defaults (157357924, describing it as `Show "Cooked for Nm Ns" after each assistant turn`), two key lists, the settings merge, the /config toggle, the settings-change log, and the RENDERER of the turn_duration message, which returns null when the setting is off (180046028) after the record has already been written; the emitter has no settings test at all. What can withhold the record is the emitter's own gate `if(O&&!I.signal.aborted)` plus a background-deferral branch (181626202): with a background task still running the record is handed to _deferSwarmDuration and emitted later by a different call site (181610437; a third emitter parks it on the async-agent keepalive path, 163877450). So the record's only conditions are main lane, not aborted, and no running background task. Corpus, measured 2026-09-04 over every transcript under the projects root, one record per matching jsonl line, with the per-file S/T marker string preserving file order: at 2.1.258 there are 48 stop_hook_summary and 48 turn_duration records over 5 transcripts (42/42, 2/2, 2/2, 1/1, 1/1), every one of the 5 marker strings is a strict S,T alternation, and all 48 turn_duration records name the IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING stop_hook_summary as parentUuid. Whole corpus on the same day: 55 files carry either subtype and 0 carry only one, totals are 5,798 stop_hook_summary against 4,791 turn_duration with 4,693 turn_duration records parented to a stop_hook_summary uuid in the same file, and per file 14 have more stop_hook_summary, 9 have more turn_duration and 32 are equal - so the 1:1 statement is a 2.1.258 statement and the corpus-wide imbalance is older builds, not this one.

Its switch (166107421) has NO default arm - an entry whose type is not in the table matches no case and is silently never written - and an `always` type is handed straight to enqueueWrite exactly as its constructor built it. That table bounds the typed-literal surface, NOT every byte that can reach a transcript: appendEntryToCurrentTranscriptNow (definition 166129659) writes an entry straight into the current session file through a synchronous O_APPEND appender (166154683, carrying the `appendEntryToExistingFileSync: short write` literal), appendEntryToFileAsync (166155592) is a second such path, both are separate exports (174412305, 174412345), three passthroughs accept any caller-built entry (166114479, 166114538, 166170820) and a test-only helper accepts any shape (166080808). Of the records that do travel the typed path, only the user record factory (165936023, `return{type:"user",message:{role:"user",content:e||up},...}`) and the assistant stream builder mint a `message{}`; the envelope stamped on every persisted line (166105359) spreads parentUuid, logicalParentUuid, isSidechain, teamName, agentName, promptId, agentId, the record itself, the cwd/sessionId/version block, gitBranch and slug, and adds no `message` key - so message-less is the default and a `message{}` is a property of two constructors rather than of the sample. FIVE message-less shapes carry the queue and telemetry facts csift promotes: `queue-operation` with the queued content (162031847), the `system` subtypes `turn_duration` (166030930), `away_summary` (166031203) and `stop_hook_summary` (166030639), and the `file-history-snapshot` / `file-history-delta` pair (166106053 / 166123148). They are a SUBSET of the message-less set, not the whole of it: `last-prompt`, `atis-latch`, `fork-context-ref`, `observer-ref`, `attribution-snapshot`, `content-replacement` and the three marble-origami types are message-less too. Corpus, measured 2026-09-04 over every transcript under the projects root, one observation per physical jsonl line bucketed by top-level type with system split by subtype, message-less meaning the parsed object has no top-level `message` key: away_summary 1,683, turn_duration 4,791, stop_hook_summary 5,798, queue-operation 13,868, file-history-snapshot 4,146, file-history-delta 2,057 - and, beyond the five, last-prompt 29,710, atis-latch 1,273 and fork-context-ref 33. That is 63,359 lines and not one of them carries a top-level `message` key. observer-ref, attribution-snapshot, content-replacement and the three marble-origami types have zero lines in this corpus, which is a corpus fact and not evidence they cannot be written.

claims.behavior: The presence of a message{} field is the one measured instrument for whether a line is part of the conversation: ZERO of 629,829 lines across the 25 measured non-record type/subtype buckets carries message{}, while every user record (229,721 of 229,721) and every assistant record (432,052 of 432,052) carries it as an object. Claude Code's own internal wording labels the promoted system subtypes render internals - turn_duration is documented as the line the REPL renders as 'Done in Ns' / 'Waiting for N agents'.

checks.rule: Gating: one observation per RECORD via `--count-by label`, run three times over the same whole-corpus scope, changing only the -t selector; a leaf is 'gated' iff it is absent from the no-selector census and present under a reaching selector. The 87% figure is right to the decimal - 8,106 of 9,276 content-bearing queue lines are automation pulses, 87.4% - and the 1,170 human-content remainder matches the user.queued census exactly, an independent cross-check. One number is wrong: 'roughly 22,000' queue lines overstates by 63%; the corpus holds 13,514 queue-operation lines, and no reading recovers 22,000 (all five promoted leaves together come to 31,470 lines). Worth recording alongside it: a queue line is written on enqueue AND on dequeue/remove, so a single pulse is counted about twice, which is part of why the queue duplicates so heavily. claims.behavior: An assistant record's `message.usage` object comes in two shapes at any one build, and which one a record carries is decided by WHEN the record was flushed, not by the build. claims.behavior: The nested `cache_creation` pair and the flat `cache_creation_input_tokens` are independent fields that very nearly partition each other but are tied by no client rule. Measured 2026-09-04 over every top-level transcript under the projects root, one observation per assistant record whose message.usage.cache_creation is a dict, missing sub-keys treated as 0, EQUAL meaning (5m or 0) + (1h or 0) == (cache_creation_input_tokens or 0): 135,782 records, 135,645 equal (99.90 percent) and 137 disagreements (0.10 percent). EVERY disagreement has ephemeral_1h_input_tokens > 0 with ephemeral_5m_input_tokens == 0 - 101 with a flat 0 and 36 with a flat above 0 - so the flat field never tracked a 1-hour cache write in those records, and none of them was written later than 2.1.252; on records written by the audited build the pair agrees on 1,886 of 1,886. The record-writing accumulator is FY (165471565), reached from the message_delta arm `wl=FY(wl,la.usage)` (165443548): it takes the API's flat value only when it is non-null AND above zero, else the nested sum when that is above zero, else the accumulator's own flat (165472012), while the nested object falls back to a DIFFERENT source, `{...e.cache_creation}` - two fallback sources, which is the in-client mechanism by which the two drift even when the API is consistent. The present-else-fallback expression `cache_creation_input_tokens: n.cache_creation_input_tokens ?? (r?(1h??0)+(5m??0):e.cache_creation_input_tokens)` belongs to Dhn (165472864), the refusal-fallback merge, NOT to the record-writing accumulator; the resulting object is stamped onto every per-block record by the fan-out (165444727) with the flat field and the nested pair side by side, never summed. No ACCOUNTING or PERSISTENCE path adds them: across all 23 occurrences of ephemeral_1h_input_tokens in the 2.1.258 binary the sites are pick-one (FY; the cache-coverage state machine Lvt at 161454209, `C=_>0?_:v`), present-else-fallback (Dhn), like-with-like sums (i9t at 165473803 and 165474158), three separate telemetry fields, templates and the schema. Exactly ONE site adds them, and it is a diagnostic threshold rather than an accounting path: the mid-conversation cache-proxy detector at 165420467 computes `bc=(cache_creation_input_tokens??0)+(cache_creation?.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens??0)+(cache_creation?.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens??0)` only to ask whether any cache write happened at all before firing api_midconv_cache_proxy. Two sites go further than the corpus rate and read the pair as a PARTITION of the flat field: the cache-write pricing function V7 (158436189) charges `Math.min(1h,flat)` at the 1-hour rate and the remainder at the 5-minute rate, and the cache-TTL cost estimator (163196513) builds a usage object with the whole flat amount in exactly one nested slot and 0 in the other.
claims.depends: Summing the nested pair alongside the flat field would double-count cache-creation tokens in `csift stats` on 99.9 percent of records; a future implementation must pick one or the other and must not assume the identity holds on every record. csift today sums only the four flat counters (src/stats.rs, the four-element `vals` array under the per-message-id per-field-MAX dedupe), so it cannot double-count; and the harness's own pricing path treats the nested 1-hour counter as a SUBSET of the flat field, which is the reading a csift implementation should copy rather than inventing an addition.
claims.instrument: Python over the mixed-version sample and over the version-current subset: for each assistant record with a dict `usage.cache_creation`, compare `(ephemeral_5m_input_tokens or 0) + (ephemeral_1h_input_tokens or 0)` against `(cache_creation_input_tokens or 0)`, and bucket the disagreements by which of the three is zero; plus `strings -n 6` over the 2.1.258 binary for the fallback expression and the pick-one expression.

The READ side is an accumulation-class table (dts, 166050484): 4 `transcript`, 8 `boundary-cleared`, 4 `accumulate`, 22 `last-wins`, and its lookup DOES default - `function fts(e){return dts[e]??"accumulate"}` (166051609). claims.behavior: Every record carries a top-level version stamp naming the build that wrote it and a gitBranch field, and both can change inside one transcript - by different mechanisms. The version stamp is a constant of the WRITING PROCESS: the per-append stamper writes version:Uts (166074085) and Uts is fixed at build time (166065151), so an in-place upgrade changes nothing for a running process and a second stamp can appear only when a NEW process adopts the same file. That happens on a NON-FORK resume: the resume handler (181936945) reaches an adoption statement guarded on the fork flag (181939450) which points the writer at the existing transcript and re-appends the session metadata (166123513, and its storage twin at 166123786); a forked resume mints a new file instead. gitBranch is read once per append (166104693) from a cache-backed getter (157762344) whose watched git state invalidates on HEAD and on refs/heads/<branch> (157784128), so it changes on any append after a checkout. Both mechanisms are version-stable across the whole range this corpus spans: the adopt path is present and byte-equivalent in every build probed from 2.1.150 to 2.1.259, so no era caveat is needed. Corpus measurement 2026-09-04 over every transcript under the projects root (7,968 files, workflow journals and the elicitation sidecar excluded): 7,967 of 7,968 carry a version stamp; 42 distinct build stamps span 2.1.150 to 2.1.259 - one build newer than the audited binary; 12 files carry more than one stamp; 29 adjacent transitions occur in physical line order and all 29 are upgrades, none a downgrade; the deepest single transcript carries 7 distinct stamps (2.1.150, 2.1.154, 2.1.156, 2.1.159, 2.1.177, 2.1.186, 2.1.191).
claims.depends: csift's list reports version and git_branch as LAST-seen with the opening values on version_first/git_branch_first plus a drift arrow (src/session/summarize.rs), and search --count-by version censuses where a new build's records begin; reporting only the opening sample was stale. Because the stamp changes only when a new process adopts the file, the first/last pair is exactly the right shape: it names the build that opened the transcript and the build writing it now.

claims.instrument: `csift search '' @<id> --count-by version` on the clone beside the same census on its origin is only SUGGESTIVE - the clone's single head version could in principle be the origin's own tail version. Counting rule = one per shared uuid; the claim holds iff origin.version != clone.version on all of them.

claims.behavior: MECHANISM. The Read tool imposes no default line window: the handler defaults offset to 1 and limit to undefined (164904193), and the shipped prompt's 'reads up to 2000 lines' sentence (160024011, the constant at 160022498) instructs the model rather than the code. The numLines/totalLines pair an echo carries has TWO producing readers, forked on isFile() && size < 10485760 (161427310): the in-memory reader (161427688) and the streaming reader (161428784 / 161430555). Equality - a FULL read - is produced by three branches, not one: the in-memory early return when offset is 0, limit undefined and neither byte budget is set (161427777); the in-memory windowed loop whenever the window happens to cover every line (161428111); and the streaming end handler's resolve on an unwindowed pass (161431048), so a full-file verdict must be stated per reader, never binary-wide. On the Read tool's own path a partial has exactly TWO causes: a caller window (an offset and/or limit narrowing the kept range - the in-memory loop's bound and the streaming reader's identical per-chunk window test at 161429390), and the token-cap re-slice (164912181), the only cause that sets truncatedByTokenCap and itself gated to an unwindowed read (164911906). The streaming reader adds no third cause: its byte-truncation arm is unreachable from Read because that call never passes truncateOnByteLimit, so an unwindowed read of a file at or above the 10,485,760-byte fork ERRORS - the stream is destroyed with the size error - instead of echoing, while a windowed read of such a file, and any read of a non-regular target, does stream and echoes normally. The measured bytes come from one literal (164914065): numLines is the kept-line count, totalLines the reader's count, and truncatedByTokenCap is spread only when the cap arm ran. PROPORTION - a usage regularity no branch of the binary produces. Measured 2026-09-04 over every transcript under the projects root, one observation per toolUseResult.file echo carrying both integer counts: 8,719 echoes, 4,888 partial (56.1 percent), 3,831 full, 0 with numLines > totalLines. 179 of the partials carry truncatedByTokenCap (3.66 percent) and 1 FULL echo carries it, the single-line clip shape. The 2026-09-04 join of each partial back to its Read tool_use input attributed 4,709 to an explicit offset and/or limit, 178 to the cap alone and 1 to both, with 0 unattributed. The corpus cannot say which reader served a given partial - the echo records a window, not a file size - but no FULL echo came from the streaming reader, the largest full echo measured being far below the fork threshold.
claims.depends: csift's replay therefore spends most of its time on `PartialRead` splices rather than full anchors, which is why the gap accounting (`??? lines A..B unknown`) and not the anchor path is `recover`'s dominant correctness surface. The two causes are distinguishable on disk - truncatedByTokenCap names the cap, and its absence on a partial means a caller window - so recover never has to guess which one clipped a read; and because equality can come from a windowed read as well as from a full-file branch, csift must read numLines == totalLines as 'this window covered the file', not as 'the caller asked for the whole file'.

claims.behavior: A tool_use and its result are joined only by the tool_use block's id echoed as the result block's tool_use_id, and the result always lands inside the same genuine-user turn as the call - by mechanism, not merely by observation. User input submitted while a turn is running never becomes a user record: the turn guard's tryStart returns null (181623439) and that arm re-enqueues every user message of the batch and returns before the batch's single append (181624300); the batch is buffered and never flushed once handed off (181586905); the queued input is drained back only while the guard is idle (181701890); and an item absorbed DURING the query is delivered as a queued_command attachment and consumed (164752640) rather than minted as a user record. Results drain back into the generator that issued the call (164583277), and the only join key written is the call id echoed on the result carrier (164578780). Corpus census 2026-09-03 over 7899 transcripts: 225906 joins resolved within one file - main 59757, subagent 35960, workflow 130189 - with 0 joins having a turn-opener candidate between call and result and 0 orphan results in every lane, 32 unreturned calls, and 14771 turn-opener candidates across 7846 of the 7899 files, so the test is not vacuous. Line ORDER within a turn is not guaranteed: 4 main-lane joins have the result line 1-2 lines BEFORE the call line (2 Edit and 2 Read; one at 2.1.156 and three at 2.1.177). One bounded exception exists in the binary: the deferred-tool / orphaned-permission resume re-emits a stored tool_use and appends its result at the current tail; it has a single call site and runs before the prompt processor mints a user record, so it cannot cross an opener, but if the resume writes to a different transcript file the call and its result are split across files and the call reads as unreturned.

The per-turn maps are sets keyed by id, built over the whole turn before any event is emitted, so the 4 reversed-order joins are harmless - order within a turn does not matter, only membership. The cross-file exception above is the one shape that would present as an unreturned call to any single-file reader, csift included.

claims.behavior: The update-side tool_result STRING is identical for a `Write` of type update and for a successful `Edit` whenever userModified is false - both then render `The file <path> has been updated successfully.` plus the shared suffix - so the result text alone cannot tell a Write from an Edit. The two templates are not byte-identical in general: Write emits `The file ${e} has been updated successfully.${f}${_}` (period before the userModified clause) while Edit emits `The file ${r} has been updated successfully${v}.${C}` (period after it), so under userModified the two texts differ, and Edit alone can substitute a staleRecovered note for the suffix. A `replace_all` Edit renders `The file <path> has been updated. All occurrences were successfully replaced.`
claims.depends: csift's input-side fallback therefore dispatches on the tool_use `name`, never on the result text: `Write` becomes a full-snapshot anchor that RESETS the reconstruction buffer while `Edit` becomes a hunk applied to it, and confusing the two would either wipe or corrupt the replay.

claims.behavior: The written payload of a file tool lives under a different input key per tool, with no shared key. In 2.1.258 the file tools and their payload keys are Write.content (schema at 163981531) and Edit.new_string (schema at 162402866), each on a file_path anchor, and NotebookEdit.new_source (schema at 164089247) on a notebook_path anchor. Each tool is shipped to the model as its own input_schema (165366520) and the model-emitted block is spread into the assistant record verbatim (165439678, 165442985), so a record's input keys are exactly that tool's schema keys. There is no MultiEdit tool in this build: no tool object and no name constant, and all 11 occurrences of the token are strings in permission, hook-matcher, path-map, deny-list and UI plumbing; the edits:[{old_string,new_string,replace_all}] literal at 162408169 is an internal helper wrapping ONE Edit hunk for the shared patch engine, not a tool input schema. Corpus census 2026-09-03 over 7899 transcripts, one observation per tool_use block: Edit 17192 blocks, every one keyed exactly {file_path, new_string, old_string, replace_all}; Write 5130 blocks, 5127 keyed {content, file_path} and 3 also carrying description; MultiEdit 0 blocks, NotebookEdit 0 blocks, new_source 0 observations. So the Write and Edit halves are attested on disk while the NotebookEdit key is schema-only here.
claims.depends: csift's wait --until 'write:<path-regex>[:<line-regex>]' (src/live/conditions.rs) matches the tool names Write, Edit, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit, reads the path from file_path else notebook_path, and scans exactly the three string-valued keys content, new_string and new_source at the TOP level of input. Two consequences hold in this build: the MultiEdit arm is an unreachable superset, harmless but dead; and because the key list is read only at the top level, any payload a future build carries under a nested key or inside an array would satisfy only the path half of the condition, never the line regex. The claim's old consequence - that a MultiEdit per-hunk edits[].new_string is unreachable to the line regex - names a shape that cannot occur here and is withdrawn.

claims.behavior: A compaction does not rewrite the transcript; it appends. On the ordinary (full) path the driver's return literal carries messagesToKeep:[] at 164836207, and the autocompact call site persists only what the assembler Wut yields - function Wut(e){return[e.boundaryMarker,...e.summaryMessages,...e.attachments,...e.hookResults]} at 164831035, called as for(let nd of Wut(xr))yield nd;pr=Fne(xr) at 164702098 - while the fuller Fne array stays in memory only. No already-written record is re-emitted, so on disk the result is a type:"system" subtype:"compact_boundary" record followed by a type:"user" isCompactSummary:true record appended after the existing lines, and every pre-compaction line number stays valid on this path. The boundary record has more than one constructor, and the set is closed: subtype:"compact_boundary" occurs at exactly SEVEN object-literal sites in the 2.1.258 binary. THREE are record-to-wire projections, keyed snake_case session_id / compact_metadata through ZVe (163585380, 169801465, 179104195). FOUR are record-shaped constructors with a camelCase compactMetadata and their own timestamp: the replay-frame ingress arm at 163579362, Ugt at 163581274, Sce at 166031952 and the frame adapter at 180225164. Exactly ONE of the four (Sce) writes isMeta, and writes it false; the other three omit the key entirely. So isMeta separates the isMeta-bearing constructor from an isMeta-LESS FAMILY of three, and no per-constructor attribution of on-disk rows follows from it. Measured 2026-09-04 over the whole projects root (8222 transcripts), one observation per compact_boundary record: 235 boundaries and 235 isCompactSummary records; the summary sits at boundary line + 1 in 235 of 235; no boundary is the first line of its file; 232 sit in top-level transcripts and 3 in child transcripts (isSidechain true, all stamped 2.1.219). Taking the nearest preceding CONVERSATION record (type user, assistant or system), 233 of 235 boundaries have a strictly older one above them, 1 has no conversation record above it at all (the clone-head shape) and 1 boundary stamped 2.1.159 has a newer user record above it. isMeta is present and false on 101 boundaries and absent on 134: among top-level rows the 98 isMeta-bearing ones are all stamped 2.1.150 through 2.1.191 and the 134 isMeta-less ones all 2.1.199 through 2.1.259, including every boundary written by 2.1.257, 2.1.258 and 2.1.259, while the 3 child-lane rows at 2.1.219 carry isMeta:false. Every observed isMeta value is false.
claims.depends: This is what lets verbatim reconstruct the clipped turns from the SAME file and lets a refetch printed before a compaction still resolve afterwards; if compaction rewrote the file, every stored Lnnnn address in a prior answer would go stale. list's clone probe leans on it too: clone_origin (src/session/summarize.rs:186-188) scans sibling transcripts in the file's own parent directory for the head boundary's uuid to join a clone to its origin, which only works because the boundary record stays where it was written in the origin. Two qualifications the ledger must keep. First, csift must never key a boundary detector on isMeta - no boundary written since 2.1.199 carries the key - and it does not: csift keys on type and subtype. Second, the line-number corollary is a property of the ORDINARY path only. Two store routines do renumber a live transcript: the local-GC compact rewrite performCompactTranscript (166098791), which is reached through requestCompact only when the store flag localGcEnabled is set (the gate at 166084451; the field defaults false at 166076591 and its only arming wrapper is called from exactly one site, the resume branch guarded by if(o.sdkUrl) at 179355990) and which additionally returns below a size floor; and the ungated tombstone removal performRemoveByUuid (166095622), which truncates the file and rewrites the tail on any session. So 'every pre-compaction line number stays valid' holds for a compaction, not for the file's whole life.

claims.behavior: Record timestamp values are NOT monotone in file order, and two located mechanisms produce the backsteps. (1) The write frontier `d5e` (166067641) walks forward and stops at the first assistant record whose `message.stop_reason` is null, so a turn still in flight is withheld and its records are appended later; the appended record keeps its ORIGINAL instant, because the transcript envelope spreads the record before its own keys (`{parentUuid,...,agentId:r,...fe,...Gjt(j),gitBranch:U,slug:W}` at 166105359) and the envelope builder `Gjt` (166074085) contributes only sessionKind, userType, entrypoint, cwd, sessionId and version - no timestamp - while `Rw` (166113243) appends in array order and consults no timestamp at all. (2) The PARTIAL compaction assembler at 163631334, whose sole call site is the summarize handler at 180780125, returns on its `from` arm `[boundaryMarker, ...messagesToKeep.map(ude), ...summaryMessages]`: the kept older records are re-emitted AFTER a boundary stamped later than they are, and the map only zeroes assistant usage, leaving uuid and timestamp intact. Measured 2026-09-04 on the deterministic sample (top-level transcripts sized 200 KB to 40 MB, 39 in the band, the newest 14 by mtime; one observation per user/assistant record with a parseable ISO timestamp; a backstep is a record more than 1 ms earlier than the running maximum of its predecessors): 11059 records, 82 backsteps (0.74%), present in 7 of the 14 files, 49 of them larger than 60 s, worst 52904.2 s (about 14.7 hours). The same recipe gave 90 backsteps in 7 files on 2026-09-02 and 92 in 8 files on 2026-09-03; the sample is mtime-dependent, so the absolute counts are snapshots and the reproducible facts are the shape - a fraction of a percent of records, present in about half the sampled files, with a long tail well past a minute.
claims.depends: `list` derives a session's first activity from a HEAD read and its last from a TAIL read (first record = earliest, last = newest; src/session/summarize.rs:20-21), and the all-projects flood-guard cap keeps the most-recently-active rows by that tail value - so a session whose tail carries a replayed or clone-copied older timestamp can be capped away or mis-sorted. `stats` is the surface that gets it right by taking a min/max over every timestamped record (src/stats.rs:240-247). Any future surface that assumes file order equals time order inherits the same defect.

claims.behavior: Claude Code serializes every transcript record with JSON.stringify and no replacer (the writer j5 at 156850249, `function j5(e){return JSON.stringify(e)+"\n"}`, selected for every queued entry by the drain at 166086450) and appends the resulting string with no encoding option, so non-ASCII text reaches disk as verbatim UTF-8 rather than as a \uXXXX escape. The ONE escape a well-formed JSON.stringify still emits for a codepoint >= U+0080 is a LONE (unpaired) surrogate, and the corpus does exhibit it. Census of the whole projects root on 2026-09-04, one observation per non-blank line bounded at the first 4,000 bytes, an escape counted only when the backslash run before the u is odd: 8,157 jsonl transcripts, 1,393,149 non-blank lines, 374,147 lines (26.86%) carrying a byte >= 0x80, 11,897 escape-regex hits of which exactly 1 is writer-emitted - a `\ud83c` left where a <persisted-output> preview was truncated mid-emoji - and the other 11,896 a literal two-character backslash-u inside quoted content. Restricted to the 68 top-level transcripts (812,882 non-blank lines) the same rule gives 181,069 non-ASCII lines (22.27%) and 0 writer-emitted escapes, reproducing the 2026-09-02 check's 67-file figures (804,007 lines, 178,918 non-ASCII, 22.25%, 0 escapes).
claims.depends: This is why csift's needle-safety predicate (json_escapes_in_string, src/search/matcher.rs) keeps non-ASCII needles prefilter-eligible, and why the product can promise regex over CJK at all: if the writer switched to ASCII-safe output, every multi-byte pattern would stop matching at the byte prefilter, before any counter could see it - the silent-drop failure `required_needles` exists to prevent. The lone-surrogate exception does not reopen that hole and is not silent. A Rust pattern cannot contain an unpaired surrogate, so no expressible needle can be lost to it; and when such a line lands, serde_json refuses the escape, so csift books the line rather than dropping it quietly - measured on 2026-09-04 with csift 0.10.3 against the single corpus specimen, `search` reports skipped_lines 1, `stats` prints "1 malformed line(s) skipped", a rendered `show --line` address bails with "no such record(s)", and `show --line N --raw` still returns the bytes.

claims.behavior: Claude Code 2.1.258 registers TWO subagent-spawning tools and accepts FOUR name strings for them. The Agent tool declares name:yt with aliases:[o_] (163908668), where var yt="Agent" and o_="Task" (159196023) - so Task is an ALIAS of the Agent tool, not a registered tool of its own; the Workflow tool declares name:Yc with aliases:["RunWorkflow"] (176145706), with var Yc="Workflow" (159837246). Tool lookup is alias-aware and does not rewrite the block: wr (159231684) falls back to e.find((n)=>an(n,o)) and an (159231331) is e.name===o||(e.aliases?.includes(o)??!1), so a tool_use block persisted on disk can carry any of the four strings and will still execute its tool. Both tools funnel into one agent runner, the async generator mT (163773651): of the 12 byte occurrences of 'mT(' in the binary, one is that definition and one is an unrelated grpc helper (188371666), leaving ten call sites of which only two are Agent-tool arms (163924599, 163928361) and one is the Workflow tool's (172627921). The other SEVEN spawn a lane with no spawning tool_use at all: an async agent launcher (163960753), a slash-command fork that reports status "forked" (163967706), a background-agent launcher (172859416), a slash-command agent path (173512022), an observer/background spawn (175695576), the in-process teammate runner (176260576) and an observer-activity spawn (187833557). The corpus carries only two of the four names: one row per tool_use block over every transcript under the projects root on 2026-09-04 (workflow journals and elicitation sidecars excluded; 8,225 files, 35 distinct tool names) gives Agent 930, Workflow 191, Task 0, RunWorkflow 0. The string list once quoted as evidence of a tool registry, var ymo=[...] at 163134741, is not one: its only use is disallowed_tools:[...ymo] in a remote review job config (163140000), a name blacklist, so it proves the STRING exists and nothing about registration.
claims.depends: csift's global spawn index and the self-to-child comm direction gate on a THREE-name set - is_spawn_tool_name (src/model/peer.rs) and is_spawn_tool (src/subagent/spawn.rs) both match only Task | Agent | Workflow - and matching only Task would leave every child unlinked and collapse the agents tree to a flat list. Two things follow from the corrected fact. The defensive Task arm stays correct, but for the alias reason rather than the registration one: a Task-named block executes the Agent tool and its name is persisted unrewritten. The fourth accepted name, RunWorkflow, is in NEITHER set, so a block carrying it would leave its children parentless and unlabelled under agent.communication.signal - the exact failure this claim's depends describes, latent today (0 RunWorkflow blocks on 2026-09-04) and closed by adding the string to both matchers. And a fourth NAME is not the only way to get a parentless lane: seven of the ten agent-runner call sites are non-tool spawn paths whose lanes carry no spawning tool_use, so csift's topology must keep tolerating a child with no issuer rather than treating one as a bug.

Either way the minted string becomes the lane id in the agent runner (Cn=B?.agentId?B.agentId:Oh() at 163774605), rides every record of that lane (163784699), and appendEntry's dedup-transcript arm routes a sidechain record carrying an agentId to Ud(uo(agentId)) (166107661), which builds agent-<id>.jsonl (159262698) - so the canonical id is exactly the file basename. Of the 165, 164 have a sibling meta with taskKind "in_process_teammate" (164/164 with no toolUseId; 135/164 with a dash strictly inside the name half) and 1 has no taskKind at all - a fork lane whose meta reads agentType "fork" with isFork true. Of Oh's two sides the unchanged-name fast path is specimen'd 165 times over and the sanitising side not at all: every one of the 165 named lanes has a name half byte-equal to its sibling meta's name field and matching Qe, which a !Qe.test(e) pass could not have left unchanged (it either strips a non-[\w-] character or truncates past 63), and no lane name on disk carries a non-word character or comes near the cap - the longest name half is 26 characters.

claims.behavior: A teammate is spawned by an `Agent` tool_use whose input.name carries the REQUESTED name and whose input.subagent_type carries the real agent type; the meta's agentType is instead overloaded with the teammate NAME, because the in-process runner builds the agent definition as O={agentType:e.agentName,...} (176256846) and keeps the real type only as customAgentType inside extraMetadata - measured equal to the meta name on 164/164 teammate metas on 2026-09-04. The meta carries no toolUseId (0/164): every meta key is a conditional spread in the sidecar write (163784844) and the teammate runner passes none, so the NAME is the only join back to the spawning record. That join is not always available, and the reason is a rename at reservation time: reserveTeammateIdentity (176285116) runs the requested name through le (176286277), which lower-cases it against the team file's existing member names and, on a collision, returns `${name}-2`, `${name}-3` and so on (the loop at 176286774); the sanitized name is what becomes identity.agentName, the lane id's name half via Oh, and the meta `name`, while the tool_use keeps the requested one. Census on 2026-09-04, one observation per teammate meta, joined against every `Agent` tool_use in the same session's main and subagent transcripts: 164 teammate metas over 11 sessions, 155 whose name appears as a spawn input.name and 9 that do not - every one of the 9 ending in -2 or -3, and one read back to its spawn shows a requested input.name against a tool_result reporting the same string suffixed -2 (written by build 2.1.196). 25 of the 472 `Agent` tool_use blocks in scope carry neither name nor subagent_type. The team lead subsequently addresses the teammate through <teammate-message> blocks and the SendMessage tool.

claims.behavior: A subagent's returned message reaches its parent by one of three carriers, not one: the synchronous tool_result text (the Agent tool's completed return at 163931233, whose payload holds the child's final assistant content), the child transcript's tail assistant text when the parent result was the async launch ack (163925044), or the workflow journal's `result` event payload - the agent() hook's closure $t at 172615720 appends {type:"result",key,agentId,result} only when a journal and a key exist and the result is not null. A node that resolves through none of the three carries a null source and no returned message, and that population has a producer: when a workflow agent's result IS null, $t routes to the failed closure $e (172615399), which appends {type:"failed"} carrying no result payload - and returns having appended nothing at all when the run's abort signal is already set - so the journal keeps a `started` event with no `result`. Measured on 2026-09-04 with csift 0.10.3 over 27 sessions and 8,084 subagent nodes, one node per subagent transcript and exactly one source per node: workflow-journal 6,548, async-child-tail 482, sync-tool-result 364, null 690. Of the 690 null-source nodes, 689 are workflow lanes and 1 is a teammate lane. Independently, the 166 workflow journals in the corpus carry 7,061 `started`, 6,372 `result` and 61 `failed` events, and exactly 689 started agent ids have no result event - 61 of them with an explicit failed event and 628 with neither.
claims.depends: csift implements all three paths and records which one answered as `returned_message_source` (src/agents/json.rs, src/agents/render.rs); dropping the async-child-tail fallback loses the report for every background-launched agent, and dropping the journal path loses it for the dominant workflow kind. A null source is not a csift miss: for a workflow lane it means the journal holds no result event for that agent, so there is nothing on disk to read - which is why the null share tracks the journals' result-less started keys one for one.

claims.behavior: The lane a completion notification is delivered to is chosen per notification; it is not fixed to the main transcript. The agent-completion enqueuer (164953374) resolves the destination first with eVe({ownerAgentId, keepaliveReason, delivering, taskRegistry}), and eVe (164954861) is a liveness decision whose last statement is `return _&&e?uo(e):Ze()` (164955053): the owner agent's OWN lane while that owner is live or its status is "running", and Ze() otherwise; the enqueued item carries that lane as agentId (164954442). The background-shell completion handler Ddt (164968006) is not liveness-gated at all - its inline enqueue addresses `agentId: v ?? Ze()` (164968716), the owning agent's lane whenever a subagent started the shell. Ze() itself (156787676) is the CURRENT lane, not a main-lane constant: it returns uo(sessionId) whenever there is an agent context and falls back to the main agent id only otherwise. Across all 56 mode:"task-notification" enqueue sites, 49 pass, default to or omit agentId:Ze() and 7 name an owner lane explicitly - one of them (163710736) with no liveness test whatever - and no site pins the destination to the main transcript. On the drain side t9e (162030912) folds per lane: the main thread takes items satisfying fg (agentId === Ze(), 160411638), a child lane takes items whose mode is task-notification and whose agentId equals its own; appendEntry then writes a sidechain record carrying an agentId to Ud(uo(agentId)) (166107661, 159262698). A child delivery is also FRAMED differently from a main one: the resume driver mints it as xe({content: dpe(d, c), origin: c, isMeta: true}) (175692385) and dpe's task-notification case (166046409) prefixes the [SYSTEM NOTIFICATION - NOT USER INPUT] block through sbt (160018067), so the tag does not sit at content start. Census on 2026-09-04, one observation per type:"user" record whose OWN message text contains the tag: 88 main transcripts hold 2,949 such records, 2,887 with the tag at content start and the same 2,887 carrying origin.kind "task-notification"; 7,908 subagent lanes hold 79, of which 0 start with the tag and 9 carry origin.kind "task-notification" - spread over 4 lane files, every one isMeta true and isSidechain true with the tag at index 494 behind the preamble, 8 written by build 2.1.252 and 1 by the audited 2.1.258. Main-lane delivery is therefore the dominant OUTCOME of a corpus whose task owners had settled, not a routing invariant.

claims.behavior: Claude Code writes `type:"system"` records for its own UI whose `subtype` falls outside the four csift models separately (`compact_boundary`, `turn_duration`, `away_summary`, `stop_hook_summary`). Measured 2026-09-04 over 8225 transcripts under the projects root (journal and elicitation-sidecar files excluded): 13087 system records under exactly 11 subtypes - stop_hook_summary 5798, turn_duration 4791, away_summary 1683, scheduled_task_fire 459, compact_boundary 235, model_refusal_fallback 51, api_error 29, local_command 15, informational 14, agents_killed 10, model_refusal_no_fallback 2. `informational` is a notice with a string `content` and a `level` (warning 9, notice 5); its live specimen is the Remote Control disconnect notice, composed at 181648256 - which also dedupes against the last transcript record - and reached from the bridge failure arm at 181655786. Every one of the 13087 carries `uuid`, `timestamp` and `parentUuid`, and NONE carries a `message{}` field. `isMeta` is NOT universal, which the old text asserted: the key is ABSENT on api_error (29 of 29), on stop_hook_summary (5798 of 5798) and on 134 of the 235 compaction boundaries, and is `false` on the remaining 7126. The constructors agree - the api_error constructor (166032184) returns {type, subtype, level:"error", error, retryInMs, retryAttempt, maxRetries, source, timestamp, uuid} with no isMeta field, and the stop_hook_summary constructor (166030639) likewise, while every other transcript-writing constructor in that cluster sets isMeta:false. A subtype the corpus has not yet seen is not guaranteed isMeta:false either: the file_snapshot record literal (163818846) writes isMeta:true. `parentUuid` is set by no system-record constructor at all - it is stamped by the shared envelope hop (166105359) after the write-policy table (166066498) routes type `system` to the transcript sink like user and assistant records - which is also why a compaction boundary is the one system record whose parentUuid is null. The 11 observed subtypes are a CORPUS property, not the shipped set: the 2.1.258 executable holds 92 adjacent `type:"system",subtype:"..."` literals over 48 DISTINCT subtype names, and the transcript-writing constructor cluster alone builds four with zero corpus specimens (permission_retry, bridge_status, cloud_session_status, memory_saved). Two of the eleven have a second literal outside that cluster and neither is a counterexample: an informational wire projection (163575905) whose only call site (179104884) spreads it into a control-protocol message carrying session_id and never appends a transcript record, and a local_command rehydration mapper (163578281) that supplies timestamp, uuid and isMeta explicitly. Only two literals in the whole executable put a `message` key inside a system-subtype object, both permission_denied (169797551, 178901181), and both are control-protocol wire projections with session_id and snake_case fields, never transcript records. The two model_refusal subtypes are inline yields in the query loop (164720173, 164725713) rather than factory functions, and model_refusal_fallback has a second producer on the banner path (164575450) that adds the `scope` key - so an audit reading only the constructor cluster would miss them.
claims.depends: `search -t harness.meta.system` (the v0.10.1 catch-all leaf, gated) classifies any system subtype other than the four modeled ones and renders `[<subtype> <level>] <content>`, falling back to `[<subtype>]` when the record carries no `level` (away_summary, turn_duration, scheduled_task_fire and agents_killed carry none; stop_hook_summary carries the unusual level `suggestion`) and to the head alone when there is no `content` (agents_killed carries neither); `show --line` renders such a line flag-free. Two csift laws rest on the record SHAPE rather than on the subtype list, which is exactly why the leaf is a catch-all and not an enumeration: the leaf is `llm_visible:false` because no such record carries a `message{}` field (0 of 13087 on 2026-09-04), and the candidate needle is the key-only `"subtype"` byte form, which admits a subtype the corpus has never seen - and 48 distinct subtype names ship against 11 observed, so it will meet one. Neither law reads `isMeta`, so the correction to that clause changes no csift code. What would break the leaf is the harness starting to send these records to the model (a `message{}` field) or moving a subtype into a differently-typed record.

On one 47,602-line transcript the naive filter reports 3,604 where csift reports 77 `user.message` records (46.8x).
claims.depends: `Record::is_genuine_user` gates on content SHAPE - a bare string, or blocks carrying a `text` block and NO `tool_result` block - and is the discriminator behind the `user.message` label, turn delimiting, `list` previews and `verbatim` reconstruction. The third sibling tag `local-command-stderr` is declared in the same tag registry (156888872) and has LIVE EMITTERS in both shapes - user records on the command-threw arms (173511115, 173530981) and the system form through the `level==="error"` selector (173525826) - so its zero records in this corpus are a sampling fact, not a structural one.

claims.behavior: Claude Code 2.1.258 ships TWO slash-command wrapper builders CONCURRENTLY and picks between them by command TYPE, not by version. The type switch in the slash-command executor (173522807, entered at 173520998) routes local and local-jsx commands through the masked wrapper helper (173531271) into the name-first builder (165937194), which emits `<command-name>/x</command-name>` first, then `<command-message>` and `<command-args>`, ALWAYS emitting the args element, with a newline plus twelve spaces of source indentation before each following tag - a byte signature that identifies this producer on disk. The `case "prompt"` arm (173526725) expands through the selector at 173532258 into the message-first builders: the prompt builder (173532119) emits `<command-message>` first, then `<command-name>/x</command-name>`, and `<command-args>` only when the argument is truthy, joined by a bare newline with no indentation; the skill twin (173531993) is also message-first, writes `<command-name>` WITHOUT the leading slash, emits no args element at all and appends `<skill-format>true</skill-format>`. All three tag constants ship in one registry (156888872); neither order is deprecated. Measured 2026-09-04 over 8225 transcripts under the projects root (journal and elicitation-sidecar files excluded; one count per user record whose string content STARTS with the tag): 166 name-first records, 166 of 166 carrying the twelve-space indentation, every one naming a built-in command (72 /model, 68 /login, 15 /compact, 5 /reload-skills, 2 /reload-plugins, 2 /effort, 1 /config, 1 /passes); against 37 message-first records, 0 of 37 indented, every one naming a prompt or a skill command, 2 of them carrying `<skill-format>` and one of those dropping the leading slash exactly as the skill builder writes it. Both orders occur at record version 2.1.258 and the name-first order at 2.1.259, which no version transition can produce. Two of the 37 message-first records carry isMeta:true while the prompt-expansion write (173537505) sets no isMeta, so those two come from another path that was not traced. Four further wrapper echoes exist as `type:"system" subtype:"local_command"` records rather than user records, so a wrapper census over user records alone is a lower bound.
claims.depends: `is_slash_command_wrapper` accepts EITHER leading tag, so a message-first wrapper is neither surfaced as genuine prose nor allowed to open a turn. Anchoring on `<command-name>` alone silently reclassified every message-first record as GENUINE user prose - raw wrapper XML surfaced as `user.message`, a no-args wrapper opened a turn, and turn NUMBERING shifted on every transcript carrying them. The corrected framing does not change that detection rule; it changes what its permanence rests on and what a census means. Accepting both leading tags is not a transition measure to be retired once the old order ages out, because both builders ship in one binary and are selected per command type: a scope with no prompt or skill commands shows zero message-first wrappers even at the newest version, which is not evidence the builder is gone. The skill form is already handled: `slash_command_name` (src/model/predicates.rs) extracts the tag body VERBATIM and never fabricates a slash, so a slash-less skill name round-trips, and because the skill builder emits no `<command-args>` the record has no args to surface and classifies `harness.command.invocation` only - the no-args path.

Whether it carries a relay preamble is decided by ONE recipient-role gate, not by a version drift: Gre (@160170310) renders each pending message into a <teammate-message teammate_id="..."> section (i7e @160170109), joins the sections with a blank line, and wraps the batch through HNe only when recipientIsLead, so a teammate receiving a message gets the BARE section (its body additionally passed through MNe) while a lead gets the wrapper; Gre always asks HNe for midTurn:!1, i.e. the colon preamble "Another Claude session sent a message:". The delivery entries are the InboxPoller idle drain (@181720788) feeding submitIncomingPrompt (@181636577, which mints with no isMeta), the in-process teammate runner (@176258096, recipientIsLead:!1), the print/headless lead drain (@179255291), and the attachment renderer Ype (@166007120), whose teammate_mailbox arm is the only teammate-family mint that sets isMeta:!0. Corpus census 2026-09-04 over every .jsonl under the projects root (8,416 files; one observation per type:"user" role:"user" record whose message.content is a STRING containing a peer open tag, bucketed by leading bytes, by which peer tag comes first, by isMeta and by whether the file sits under a subagents path): 909 records. 862 have <teammate-message> as their first tag and isMeta false on every one - 464 begin with the bare tag and every one of those sits in a subagent (teammate) lane, 390 begin with the colon preamble and every one of those sits in a main lane, and 8 carry the tag only mid-prose (the quoted case the section-boundary test exists for). The remaining 47 are the <agent-message> delivery family of TURN-016: isMeta true on every one, 29 under the mid-turn preamble in subagent lanes and 18 under the colon preamble in main lanes. The bare-versus-preamble split therefore follows Gre's recipient ternary lane for lane; no teammate-family record in this corpus carries the mid-turn preamble, and Ype's teammate_mailbox arm has zero specimens. The preamble literals sit in one var statement (@160139849) that declares the base string, the mid-turn form, the colon form and "A peer session sent a message while you were working:", and B6 (@160142677) holds all three with trailing newlines; HNe (@160143654) can build only the mid-turn or the colon form, so the fourth is a RECOGNITION prefix, never an emitted preamble (TURN-016 enumerates its consumers; 0 corpus specimens). claims.behavior: The <agent-message from="..."> peer form is minted by the SendMessage in-process delivery path (@175782378), which wraps the outgoing body with the element template tge (@158150810: an open tag carrying the sanitised from attribute, the masked body, and the close tag) whenever a sender task id and a from-name are both known, and mints a delivery origin {kind:"peer",from,senderTaskId,...}. Both delivery lanes stamp isMeta:!0 (@175782784): case main enqueues into the session command queue and the record is prefixed post-mint by whn (kind peer -> HNe midTurn:!1, @166048114) at the prompt mint mc (@169779835), giving the COLON preamble; case agent-live pushes into the target agent's pendingMessages, rendered by dpe (case peer -> HNe midTurn:!0, @166046708) at the queued_command attachment arm (@166013419) and at the agent resume seed (@175692385), giving the MID-TURN "while you were working" preamble. The record itself is the ordinary user envelope xe (@165936023): type "user", message.role "user", content the string, isMeta from the caller. Claude Code 2.1.258 DEFINES three relay preambles in one var statement (@160139849) and STRIPS all three as one list, B6 (@160142677), but EMITS only two of them: HNe's ternary (@160143879) can produce only the colon or the mid-turn form. "A peer session sent a message while you were working:" has exactly two references in its chunk - its declaration (@160139943) and its B6 membership - is absent from the chunk export list (@160187292), and every B6 consumer read is a startsWith/slice recogniser or stripper, so it is recognition-only, never emitted, with zero corpus specimens. Corpus census 2026-09-04 over every .jsonl under the projects root (8,416 files; one observation per type:"user" role:"user" record whose message.content is a STRING and whose FIRST peer tag is <agent-message>, i.e. the delivery family): 47 occurrences over 46 distinct record uuids (one record copied into two transcripts), isMeta true on every one - 29 mid-turn-preamble records in subagent (sidechain) lanes and 18 colon-preamble occurrences over 17 distinct records in main lanes. The counting rule is load-bearing: a rule of "records CONTAINING the tag" returns 64 occurrences, the extra 17 being teammate relays whose body quotes it.

Keying peer detection off isMeta drops the form entirely; carrying only the colon preamble drops every mid-turn relay into the empty label vector - no turn, no leaf, no census row, no rendered show address, only show --raw - which is what csift 0.10.0 through 0.10.2 did to the 29 mid-turn records, fixed in 0.10.3. claims.behavior: A peer open tag is written only at a section boundary, and the preamble is the minority head rather than the frame of the rule. One writer emits a single section as "<teammate-message teammate_id=\"...\"[ color][ summary]>" newline body newline "</teammate-message>" (160170109), and the join site maps every message through it and joins the sections with a blank line, wrapping the joined string only when the recipient is the lead (160170310) - so a later section's open tag is separated from the previous close tag by exactly a blank line, and the FIRST tag sits either after a single preamble line or at content start. The preamble set is measured rather than counted: one function refuses to double-prefix an already-wrapped batch and then selects the mid-turn or the colon head, plus a host-injected suffix and a descendant-lineage variant, or, for an activity observation, a separate head pair (160143654), with all of those constants in one table beside the recognition-only peer form (160139849). It has four call sites: the join site (only when the recipient is the lead), the origin-driven applier that the prompt record builder calls at mint time from both arms of its content-shape branch (166048114, called at 169779782 and 169779946), the mid-turn framing selector's peer arm (166046259), and a model-context assembler that pushes bare {role,content} objects and writes no transcript record (165542711). Head distribution on 2026-09-04 over the projects root: of 909 peer-tag string-content user records, 464 carry NO preamble at all (the not-lead path), 408 the colon form, 29 the mid-turn form and 8 ordinary prose. Batching is real, not hypothetical: on 2026-09-02, 125 records carried a section open tag immediately after a close tag (123 after a teammate close, 2 after a task-notification close).
claims.depends: csift recognises a tag only at a SECTION BOUNDARY - the content start, immediately after the COLON-form relay preamble, or right after a prior section's close tag (src/model/peer.rs) - so a batched record still yields every section while a quoting message stays user.message instead of being reparented to agent.communication.inbox or a harness notification. Content start already covers the preamble-less majority, which is the largest head bucket; the two "while you were working" preambles are the gap in the boundary set and are recorded under TURN-016.

claims.behavior: A subagent transcript's FIRST record is an isSidechain:true type:"user" seed carrying the spawn prompt. The Agent tool's call handler (163908866) takes the non-fork arm of the seed-builder branch (163919675) and mints exactly one string-content user record; the chain is handed to insertMessageChain with isSidechain hardcoded true (166114240), the envelope literal stamps isSidechain and agentId onto every record (166105359), and appendEntry's dedup-transcript arm routes such a record to the per-agent file (166107780) - so a sidechain seed can never land in a top-level transcript. A FORK child instead leads with a type:"fork-context-ref" line carrying exactly agentId, parentSessionId, parentLastUuid and contextLength, written on the runner's fork branch (163784470); but its directive seed does NOT follow immediately. ONE flag in the Agent tool - the subagent_type resolves to the fork type (constant at 159196188) AND that type is available (163910331) - selects BOTH the fork seed builder and the forkContextMessages argument (163921718) that alone can satisfy the fork-head branch's identity test, and the builder (163882619, returning at 163883130) returns TWO records: a re-minted copy of the parent's last assistant message (new uuid, content array copied) and a user record holding one tool_result per copied tool_use carrying the template that opens "Fork started" plus the fork directive text; only the degenerate no-tool_use arm returns a single record, and even that is a text-BLOCK array. So the record after a fork head is an ASSISTANT record and the child's directive seed is the THIRD record. The runner concatenates the inherited context ahead of the child's own messages (163774706), so the fork branch's slice drops the inherited PREFIX and keeps the child's own records; the assistant-first ordering comes from the seed builder, not from the slice. That coupling is NOT recent: the identical two-record builder and the identical one-flag coupling are present in every cached build read - 2.1.191, 2.1.215, 2.1.216, 2.1.219, 2.1.221, 2.1.222, 2.1.224, 2.1.228, 2.1.232, 2.1.233, 2.1.251 and 2.1.258 - so the fork head and the two-record seed cannot be separated through the Agent tool's fork arm in any of them, and the single contrary corpus lane has no identified producer. claims.behavior: When the user recalls a sent message with escape, edits it and re-sends, Claude Code leaves the ORIGINAL on disk: the draft and the delivered resend are separate `type:"user"` records sharing ONE non-null `parentUuid`, and only the last in file order was delivered. The shared parent is usually a turn-end anchor record - measured parents were a `stop_hook_summary` system record 133 times, `turn_duration` 83, `away_summary` 80, an interrupt marker 19 and an assistant record once.
claims.depends: `superseded_draft_indices` keeps the LAST opener per `parentUuid` and marks the earlier siblings superseded, and `group_turn_indices_deduped` drops them entirely from turn numbering, so an edited-away message can never resurface as a phantom turn or leak its abandoned text into a neighbour. The signal is parent-uuid IDENTITY, not text similarity, which would miss the common prepend/insert edit; distinct real turns never share a parentUuid, and a record with a null/empty parent is never grouped.
claims.instrument: Group all turn-opening user records of one transcript by `parentUuid` and count groups of size greater than one (counting rule: drafts = group size minus one, one per group), then cross-validate against csift's own `N superseded draft(s)` footer. claims.behavior: Two neighbouring shapes leave no user record, and they differ in evidential standing. (a) THE QUEUE HALF is fully written. A queued text edited before dispatch never becomes a type:"user" record: the REPL submit dispatcher enqueues every typed prompt and returns early while a turn is running (181580347); the admission gate pushes the item and logs it only when the item is not marked unlogged and only when its value is a string (162035115); the writer builds {type:"queue-operation", operation, timestamp, sessionId, content?, reason?} (162031901) and hands it to the default sink, which ends in insertQueueOperation and appendEntry with queue-operation routed "always" (162029731). The two escapes are the drain that logs each item and returns the joined text to the INPUT BOX without constructing any message record (162041220), and the mid-turn fold, which emits the item as a queued_command attachment and consumes it with reason "absorbed_mid_turn" (164752627). So the typed text survives only in the queue-operation lines. Corpus on 2026-09-04: 39 transcripts carry parsed type:"queue-operation" lines - enqueue 6,924 (all with content), popAll 109 (all with content), dequeue 3,534 (none), remove 3,273 of which 2,477 carry content. Of the enqueues, 949 are human prose (content not opening with "<"); whitespace-normalized, 610 of those match a later user record in the same file exactly (64.3 percent), 126 more match by their first 200 characters (13.3 percent, 77.6 percent combined) and 213 never match (22.4 percent). (b) THE ESC-RECALL HALF is a negative closed by enumeration, not a written path. The local recall entry rewinds and then puts the recalled text back into the input box (180778537); the rewind itself slices the in-memory snapshot and replaces it with no append anywhere (180776684), and the transcript file is append-only, so the recalled message's own record stays exactly as written and nothing new is written. At 2.1.258 a rewind CAN leave one positive artifact - a last-prompt line carrying leafUuid and rewound:true (166113611) - but it names the rewind event and the surviving leaf, never the recalled text, and of the six occurrences of that function name exactly one is the definition, four are call sites and one is an unrelated same-named component; only the remote/bridge rewind handler passes the flag, building {rewound:true} and handing it to both the internal-event mirror and the transcript append (179289648). In this corpus that marker has zero specimens: 0 lines carry it against 29,662 last-prompt lines on 2026-09-04. So the recalled text is never re-written, and no rewind marker exists here at all.
claims.depends: csift's user.unsent covers only SUPERSEDED drafts - the esc-recall and edit-resend pairs detected by a shared parentUuid (src/model/grouping.rs) - never "every unsent message". The queue-only class is a separate and larger set, reachable solely under the gated user.queued leaf, and csift documents the join rule and its counting basis instead of asserting a bare dispatched flag: the queue-operation line carries no join key, and roughly a fifth to a quarter of enqueued human prose never becomes a user record. A message recalled and then abandoned has no sibling and stays undetectable from the local path, which writes nothing; the version-scoped caveat is that a rewind driven through the remote/bridge handler can write a rewound:true last-prompt line, so if such a line ever appears in a corpus csift reads, that half has to be re-decided rather than re-asserted - the line names the surviving leaf, which would give csift a second instrument for abandoned branches.
claims.instrument: Extract every `queue-operation` enqueue `content` and test whether the whitespace-normalized text appears as a later `type:"user"` record's string content or `text` block - `csift search '' @<id> -t user.queued --format json` against `-t user.message`. Counting rule: enqueue lines only, human prose only, one comparison per enqueued text; 'exact' = full-string equality, 'prefix' = the first 200 characters as a substring. An earlier figure of about 61% never-dispatched (54 of 88 texts, three-session sample) was measured over ALL queue operations and is superseded by the human-prose-only figures.

claims.behavior: Claude Code resolves its config home in ONE memoized expression and never branches on a platform to do it: (process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ?? join(homedir(), '.claude')).normalize('NFC'), with the projects root being join(<config home>, 'projects'). The expression is byte-identical in the darwin-arm64 and the win32-arm64 artifacts of 2.1.258 (win32 @172652965; that module imports the home lookup from the runtime os module at @172651975), and there is no HOME test, no USERPROFILE test and no platform switch anywhere on that path. An exclusion sweep of the win32 artifact's eleven other sites naming either variable found none of them on the config-home path: two vendored dependencies resolving their OWN config directory under AppData/Roaming, a generated environment-name accessor table, a settings/env allowlist, a WSL desktop-path builder, an IDE-lockfile discovery that again joins the runtime home lookup, a PowerShell probe that prints the profile directory for WSL IDE detection only, a shell-executable search, an expander for user-typed %USERPROFILE%/%HOMEDRIVE%/%HOMEPATH% strings, two spawn env allowlists, and one honest false positive - a vendored dependency resolving its own cache directory as HOME || USERPROFILE || HOMEDRIVE+HOMEPATH. The per-platform home split is therefore a property of the JavaScript RUNTIME, not of Claude Code: the win32 artifact's os module forwards homedir straight to a native binding (@79996700, beside a hardcoded platform 'win32' and type 'Windows_NT'), so no shipped JavaScript in any Claude Code build can show which variable that lookup prefers. The documented semantics of that lookup are $HOME on unix and the profile directory on Windows; the unix half reproduces on this host (an overridden HOME is what comes back), and the Windows half has not been decided by a divergent-HOME trial here.
claims.depends: csift's home_dir() (src/path/home.rs) is cfg-split to mirror those same os.homedir() semantics - unix reads HOME, Windows reads USERPROFILE, with the standard library's home lookup as the fallback - and then joins '.claude' behind the same $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR override the binary applies first (csift's precedence being --claude-home > $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR > the OS home's .claude). So a POSIX-style HOME exported by a Windows shell never sends csift to a .claude directory Claude Code does not write; honoring it there would make every subcommand read an empty or nonexistent projects root. The dependency is on the RUNTIME's home resolution, not on a Claude Code platform branch: there is none to track, and what would break csift is that runtime changing which variable it prefers on Windows, not a change in Claude Code.
