claims.behavior: The session registry row <claude-home>/sessions/<pid>.json stamps the owner process's creation instant under ONE key, unconditionally: the row literal is {pid, sessionId, cwd, startedAt, procStart: await <procStartGetter>(process.pid), version, ...} in both artifacts of 2.1.258 (win32 @174703780, darwin @158819044). The row writer never calls the two-key splitter. The RENDERING is platform- and capability-dependent, and on Windows there are TWO incompatible ones: the acquisition (win32 @174020355) returns the raw creation FILETIME as a decimal string (100ns ticks since 1601-01-01, read from OpenProcess + GetProcessTimes through an in-process foreign-function binding to kernel32, epoch constant 116444736000000000n @174015383) when that binding loads, and otherwise spawns powershell with (Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "ProcessId=<pid>").CreationDate.Ticks, which renders .NET ticks since year 1 - roughly 6.4e17 today against the FILETIME's 1.34e17. The darwin acquisition (@158136222) has only the ps -o lstart= -p <pid> arm with LC_ALL=C and TZ=UTC, so it yields the asctime form (Sun Aug 16 09:04:23 2026); the darwin capability predicate is the constant false at @158132377, which is why that build contains no tick producer at all. The binary encodes the two-rendering fact itself: a tolerance treats two proc-start values on opposite sides of 3e17 as the SAME process (win32 @174018881), gated on the same capability predicate. A SECOND key, procStartFt, does exist, but on OTHER payloads: a platform-conditional splitter (win32 @174019832, darwin @158135690) writes the value to exactly one of procStart/procStartFt and has exactly six call sites, none of them the registry row - two messaging key-companion writers, an in-use marker payload, a worktree lock-reason string that reads only the procStart half, a daemon/supervisor lock record, and a job-holder identity that renames the pair to holderProcStart/holderProcStartFt. Its paired reader is NOT procStartFt ?? procStart: on the FILETIME-capable platform it REFUSES a record carrying procStart and returns procStartFt only, otherwise it returns procStart (win32 @174019733, darwin @158135600), and its eleven win32 call sites inherit that refusal. What does accept both keys is the registry row READER (darwin @159696721, field handling at ~@159697150: procStart taken when it is a string, procStartFt spread in when it is one). Specimen: a Windows 11 ARM64 session at 2.1.258 wrote an 18-digit value under procStart with no procStartFt and pidDomain 'win32:<host>'; decoded as a FILETIME it lands 166.3 s before that row's own startedAt, decoded as .NET ticks it lands in year 427, so that row came from the FILETIME path. On this unix host, 2026-09-04: 4 of 4 rows carry the asctime form, 0 all-digit, 0 procStartFt (counting rule: one classification per <pid>.json row file; an all-ASCII-digit value is a tick rendering).
claims.depends: csift reads procStartFt first and falls back to procStart - a superset of what the row writer emits, so the read order stays safe even though the binary's own paired reader is not a ?? fallback - then parses the value into an instant and compares it with the probed process start within a 2-second tolerance: an all-ASCII-digit value is decoded as a FILETIME, anything else through the asctime parse. That mapping covers the unix asctime form and the Windows FILETIME form, and it is WRONG for the Windows PowerShell-fallback rendering: .NET ticks decoded as a FILETIME land about sixteen centuries out, blow the 2-second tolerance, and make probe_pid return Reused, which the verdict layer renders as 'pid reused by another process' - a live session reported dead, on exactly the Windows hosts where the foreign-function binding does not load. The code that relies on the old mapping: parse_registry_proc_start and filetime_to_timestamp (src/live/registry.rs 175-199), the comparison arm at src/live/registry.rs 143-152, the module doc at src/live/registry.rs 13-21 whose platform story is one rendering per platform, and the row-read comment at src/live/registry.rs 72-77, which states that every reader in the binary is procStartFt ?? procStart. Reading a single key, or parsing a single format, would still silently degrade a Windows row to a disclosed pid-only probe; the new failure the trace exposes is worse than a degrade, because a mis-decoded value is not unparseable and so is not disclosed at all.

claims.behavior: Process liveness has no portable probe, and the host-utility half of this claim is a property of the operating systems rather than of Claude Code: on unix ps -p PID -o lstart= answers both existence and start time, except that a minimal userland's ps rejects -p/lstart outright and so fails even for a LIVE pid, where Linux /proc/<pid> answers liveness directly; Windows ships no such ps. What the audited binary itself does, read in both artifacts of 2.1.258: existence is process.kill(pid, 0) on every platform (win32 @174015796), and the start time is acquired per platform - unix by LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC ps -o lstart= -p <pid> (darwin @158134674), Windows by a kernel32 OpenProcess + GetProcessTimes read of the raw creation FILETIME through an in-process foreign-function binding, with a spawned (Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "ProcessId=<pid>").CreationDate.Ticks as the fallback, whose rendering is .NET ticks since year 1 and not a FILETIME (win32 @174018594 and @174020355, capability gate @174014790). The harness uses NEITHER Get-Process -Id NOR a task listing for liveness. Enumerated 2026-09-04: Get-Process occurs 6 times in the win32 artifact and 5 in the darwin one, and the only application-code sites in either are a shell alias-table entry (win32 @177403950) and a permission-prompt placeholder (win32 @196979830); tasklist occurs 6 times in each, every one of them a markdown-extension name list, a shell command-name table, an IDE-detection pipe into findstr (win32 @92595224 and @176137451), a safe-flag allowlist (@191534400) or a command allowlist (@191559223). The /proc reader returns undefined off linux and wsl (win32 @174015876), and the process-group kill is stubbed to false on Windows (@174016806). The darwin artifact contains none of the Windows instruments (Get-CimInstance 0 occurrences, ToFileTimeUtc 0, the win32 proc-times log tag 0, against 9 / 0 / 4 in the win32 artifact), which is why an earlier read of the mac build alone concluded that no Windows probe existed.
claims.depends: csift's probe is its OWN platform chain - deliberately not the harness's - and it never fabricates a verdict: unix tries ps -p PID -o lstart= then /proc/<pid>; Windows runs one PowerShell script that answers both questions (Get-Process -Id failing with the script's exit 3 for a missing pid, StartTime.ToFileTimeUtc() for the creation FILETIME, a NOSTART sentinel when another user's process hides it) and then falls back to tasklist /FI "PID eq <pid>" for existence alone; and when no probe tool exists - including on a host that is neither unix nor Windows - the verdict is Unavailable, stating that pid liveness cannot be checked here rather than reporting a live session stale-dead. Because csift reads a FILETIME while the harness may have written its .NET-ticks fallback rendering into the same procStart key, the two can disagree on a Windows host where the foreign-function binding does not load; that consequence belongs to the proc-start claim, and the binary's own 3e17 straddle tolerance is the harness's own answer to it. Nothing in csift depends on the harness using the same instruments - only on the host utilities behaving as described - so a change of harness probe does not move csift; a change in the host utilities does.

                "probe unavailable on this host".to_string(),
                Some("pid liveness cannot be checked here - stale-dead is undecidable".to_string()),
            ),

claims.instrument: On macOS ps -p $$ -o lstart= prints the LOCAL-zone instant in the '%a %e %b %H:%M:%S %Y' field order (day of month before month), which is csift's SECOND parse format - the registry's own procStart, written with TZ=UTC, uses the '%a %b %e ...' order instead. A probe test that pins only one order will pass on one platform and silently fall back to Alive(None) on the other. A missing pid is reported by a non-zero ps exit, not an empty stdout.

claims.behavior: Claude Code 2.1.258 synthesizes the AskUserQuestion tool_result in `mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam` from the result object `{questions, answers, response?, annotations?, afkTimeoutMs?}` (the tool's `call()` copies these from the answered tool input; `response` and `afkTimeoutMs` are written only when set) by a fixed branch order: `afkTimeoutMs` set -> `No response after Ns - the user may be away from keyboard ...`, plus `Before going idle the user had selected: <pairs>.` when any answer pair exists; else `response` non-blank -> `The user responded: <response>`; else any answer pair -> `Your questions have been answered: <pairs>. You can now continue with these answers in mind.` when every question was answered by a listed label with no notes, otherwise `The user answered: <pairs>. Read the answers carefully - they may request clarification, changes, or that you not proceed - and follow what they actually say.`; else `The user did not answer the questions.` A pair renders `"q"="a"`, or `"q"=(no option selected)` when `answers[q]` is the sentinel `(notes only)`, with ` notes: ...` and `selected preview: ...` suffixes from `annotations[q]`. The TUI dialog's submit function returns `updatedInput = {...input, answers, annotations, afkTimeoutMs?}` and never writes `response`: the `Other` entry stores the typed text as `answers[q]`, a notes-only submission stores the `(notes only)` sentinel, `Chat about this` is not an answer at all (it denies the tool use with the `The user wants to clarify these questions.` template, recorded as an `is_error` tool_result), and the idle path is armed by the `askUserQuestionTimeout` setting / `CLAUDE_AFK_TIMEOUT_MS` (default never).
claims.depends: csift recognises an AskUserQuestion answer by EITHER structured signal - a non-empty `toolUseResult.answers` (`has_auq_answers`) OR a present, non-blank `toolUseResult.response` (`has_auq_response`, v0.10.3) - and by the start-anchored text markers as the fallback for carriers without `toolUseResult`; so every shape the TUI produces (a label, an `Other` text, a notes-only sentinel, a partial selection at idle timeout) AND the `response`-only shape (`answers` = {} and the text `The user responded: ...`) classify `user.answer` and open a turn, the `response` shape rendering the questions asked plus a `response:` line in the AUQ unit, and the `Chat about this` deny classifies `user.rejection`. The idle-timeout text with no answer pair (`No response after ...`, `afkTimeoutMs` set) matches no marker and opens no turn. 0.10.0-0.10.2 required a non-empty `answers` and lacked the `The user responded:` prefix, so the `response`-only carrier classified `agent.tool.result` and opened no turn.
